terms.comment: Lewis & Short (s.v. ha): “an exclamation of laughter or derision”; written as one word or three, -hae or -he.

phrases.latin: Ha ha hae! — Quid rīsistī? — Servī vēnēre in mentem Syrī calliditātēs.
phrases.english: Ha ha ha! — What are you laughing at? — Syrus the slave’s tricks came into my mind.

phrases.latin: Hahahae, jam teneō quid sit, perspexī modo.
phrases.english: Ha ha, now I get it; I’ve just seen through it.

sources: Lewis & Short: ha (hahae, hahahae)

Plautus, Terence and Cicero’s letters checked against the Perseus Latin texts (Plautus ed. Leo, with its line numbers; Terence ed. Parry, whose line numbers can run one off the OCT’s; lines taken from the loci collections are cited by the OCT’s; Cicero’s letters ed. Purser).
